Founded
FOWN-ded
v. (past, pp.)
From Latin fundare, to lay a bottom or base, from fundus, bottom. Webster 1828: set; established; fixed firmly. In the Authorized Version God is the subject: He founded the earth, He founded Zion, He founded His testimonies for ever — and our Lord ends the Sermon on the Mount with a house founded upon a rock.

Biblical Definition

Founded in Scripture is what God does that afterwards holds. The creation is described in the verb: he hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods (Psalm 24:2); as for the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them (Psalm 89:11); The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he established the heavens (Proverbs 3:19). Even the valleys are where He put them — the waters go down by the valleys unto the place which thou hast founded for them (Psalm 104:8). The same verb secures His word: Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old that thou hast founded them for ever (Psalm 119:152). And it secures His people’s refuge: the LORD hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it (Isaiah 14:32) — a foundation laid, and the poor named as those who take shelter on it. Our Lord closes His great sermon with the word and puts it to a test: the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock (Matthew 7:25). The difference between the two houses is invisible until the storm, and it is entirely below ground.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines FOUNDED as set; fixed; established on a basis; and FOUND, as a verb, to lay the basis of anything; to set or place on a permanent basis.

expand to see more

FOUND, v.t. [L. fundo, fundare; fundus, bottom.] — To lay the basis of any thing; to set, or place, as on something solid for support.

To begin and build; to lay the foundation and raise a superstructure; as, to found a city.

To establish on a basis; to fix firmly.

FOUNDED, pp. — Set; fixed; established on a basis; begun and built.

Webster’s fixed firmly is the biblical force. A thing founded is not merely started; it is set on something that will bear it, and the whole question in Matthew 7 is what that something is.

Key Scripture

Psalm 24:2 — "For he hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods."

Psalm 89:11 — "The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: as for the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them."

Psalm 119:152 — "Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old that thou hast founded them for ever."

Isaiah 14:32 — "What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the LORD hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it."

Matthew 7:25 — "And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock."

Modern Corruption

Matthew 7:25 is corrupted when the rock is made anything other than what our Lord says it is — hearing His sayings and doing them — and Psalm 119:152 whenever the permanence of God’s testimonies is traded for the assumption that later ages revise earlier ones.

expand to see more

Our Lord identifies the rock in the preceding verse: Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock (Matthew 7:24). The foundation is not sincerity, not religious feeling, not attendance, and not doctrinal knowledge held without obedience — the foolish builder in the parable heard the same sermon. Nor is this works-righteousness: the same chapter has just warned that many will say Lord, Lord and be told I never knew you, so the issue is a real relation to Christ that produces doing. James says it in his own idiom: be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves (James 1:22). The storm does not create the difference; it reveals a difference already there and invisible.

Psalm 119:152 is the other foundation and it is under different pressure. Thou hast founded them for ever is said of God’s testimonies, and it is incompatible with the assumption that Scripture’s moral teaching is a record of an earlier stage that later generations improve upon. The historical-critical enterprise, and the progressive theology built on it, both require the testimonies to be founded in a time and revisable with the times. The psalmist says he has known of old that they were founded for ever — and Paul’s foundation language points the same way: other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 3:11), and the foundation of God standeth sure (2 Timothy 2:19).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The Hebrew yasad means to found or establish, and its noun is a foundation; the Greek themelioo in Matthew 7:25 is from themelios, a foundation stone.

expand to see more

Hebrew yasad (H3245) — to found, establish, lay a foundation; Psalm 24:2, 89:11, 119:152; Proverbs 3:19; Isaiah 14:32.

Hebrew mosad and yesod — a foundation; the nouns from the same root, used of the temple and of the earth’s pillars.

Greek themelioo (G2311) — to lay a foundation, to found; it was founded upon a rock (Matthew 7:25), and rooted and grounded in love (Ephesians 3:17).

Greek themelios (G2310) — a foundation stone; other foundation can no man lay (1 Corinthians 3:11), the foundation of God standeth sure (2 Timothy 2:19).

Greek petra (G4073) — a rock, bedrock, as against psammos, sand; the contrast that decides both houses in Matthew 7.

Usage

"The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth (Proverbs 3:19) — creation described as a foundation laid."

"Thou hast founded them for ever (Psalm 119:152) — God’s testimonies fixed, not revisable by later ages."

"It fell not: for it was founded upon a rock (Matthew 7:25) — the difference between two houses is below ground until the storm."
